items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I got to meet all my old heroes on those records, like Lawrence Brown was there

ctx.x: Yeah, I think we did some nice ballads with Joe. We had an orchestra with strings and we did some small group things. That was one of the great things about doing the studio work was that along with all of the garbage that they throw at you, there is all these wonderful people coming through New York all the time to make records and I think he did this nice album — Joe Hunter wrote the arrangements. And right shortly after I arrived in New York City, in 1954, Buck Clayton was contracted to do these jam session…

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Irvie Green, and there was -- well, all of the big timers usually did a stint there one time or another.

ctx.x: Irvie Green, and there was -- well, all of the big timers usually did a stint there one time or another. And, oh yes, Godfrey -- we also did the Godfrey show. Oh, many, many, many shows over a period of four years. And all of the big movie stars would do a guest appearances. You got to see everything, and experience a stint of doing a turn with all these big performers.
And you said during that time you did do some recording. Who did you record (with) during that period?
